findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, with confusing dead logic
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(...)`, then returns false in both branches. SQL expressions are therefore disabled unconditionally, even with the feature flag on. That matches the security intent, but the inverted `enabled` variable and the redundant branches suggest a bug and make the code hard to review. It should be a plain `return false`, or the call site should return the error directly, with a comment explaining the intentional hard-disable.

findings.title: Disabling is only enforced in ReadQuery; other construction paths are not guarded
findings.body: Only the ExpressionQueryReader path rejects SQL queries. UnmarshalSQLCommand and NewSQLCommand are still reachable, for example through the legacy node-building path in the pipeline. They call sql.TablesList, which now returns a 'not implemented' error and surfaces as a generic 'error reading SQL command'. The behavior is inconsistent, and the user-facing message differs by path. The disabling should be applied centrally, for example in NewSQLCommand.

findings.title: No tests cover the disabled behavior
findings.body: The PR adds stub DB methods and a hard-disable but no tests asserting that SQL expression queries are rejected. Existing SQL command/parser tests that depended on DuckDB may now fail or be silently stale. A regression test is needed to guard against re-enabling the vulnerable path.
